Where the test data for the Home Assistant source comes from.

Captured from running software
------------------------------
A Home Assistant Core 2026.11.2 container (ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:2026.11.2,
"default_config:" and "demo:" in configuration.yaml), started only for this on a workstation on
2026-11-18 and removed afterwards. gen/capture.sh has the commands, gen/backup.py is what it runs
inside the container to make an automatic backup, gen/fixtures.py turned the captures into the
files here.

config.json               GET /api/config, as answered.
states-container.json     GET /api/states, all 124 entities, after: "update.skip" on one demo
                          entity; one automatic backup that worked and one that failed (asked
                          for through the websocket API with an agent that does not exist); two
                          template update entities added, one unavailable and one with no
                          latest version; a restart. As answered, except that the access tokens
                          of the demo cameras are replaced by zeros.
states-first-start.json   GET /api/states right after the first start: updates waiting, no
                          backup yet.
states-installing.json    GET /api/states 2.5 seconds into "update.install" on the demo entity
                          with progress, after the skip.
states-backup-ok.json     GET /api/states after the automatic backup that worked.
                          These three keep only the update entities, the backup integration's
                          entities, sun.sun and zone.home; each kept entity is byte for byte as
                          answered.
unauthorized.txt          The body of the 401 for a wrong token. The status and the headers the
                          test server sends with it are the captured ones too.

Built by hand
-------------
A container has no Supervisor, so its entities could not be captured. gen/fixtures.py builds
them in the shape of the captured update entities, with the values that
homeassistant/components/hassio/update.py (titles, pictures, release links, features),
esphome/update.py, uptime_kuma/update.py and hacs/integration's custom_components/hacs/update.py
give them. Versions are the ones current on 2026-11-18 (Core 2026.11.2, Supervisor 2026.11.0,
Home Assistant OS 18.5); app and device names are examples.

states-haos.json                 Home Assistant OS: Core, operating system and Supervisor, four
                                 apps, an integration from HACS, an Uptime Kuma instance, two
                                 ESPHome devices, and the backup sensors with states of a
                                 schedule on Monday and Thursday.
states-haos-backup-running.json  The backup entities of the same installation while an automatic
                                 backup runs.
config-haos.json                 config.json with the version of that installation and "hassio"
                                 among the components.
config-starting.json             config.json with state "STARTING".

Not captured anywhere: a real Home Assistant OS installation, the Supervisor's proxy
(http://supervisor/core/api) and what it answers to an app without "homeassistant_api: true".
The test for that path uses a 401, which is an assumption.
